record.context_brief: Infinitely many periods with stable bov
record.original_question: For a meromorphic function with a stable Baker omitted value, can there be infinitely many Herman rings whose periods vary, even though for each fixed period p >= 3 the number of p-periodic Herman rings is known to be finite? In particular, can this happen when the Baker omitted value is the only accumulation point of the critical values?

evidence.quote: Theorem 5.11. Let f be a function with a stable bov and p >= 3. Then the number of p-periodic Herman rings is finite.

For a function with a stable bov and fixed p >= 3, Theorem 5.11 proves that the number of p-periodic Herman rings is finite. However, this result does not exclude the possibility of the function having infinitely many Herman rings of different periods. Whether such a situation can occur, particularly when the bov is the only accumulation point of the critical values, remains an open question.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let f be a transcendental meromorphic function on the complex plane. An omitted value of f is a point a ∈ ℂ such that f(z) ≠ a for all z ∈ ℂ. An omitted value a is called a Baker omitted value (bov) of f if there exists an open disk D centered at a such that every connected component of the boundary of f^{-1}(D) is bounded in ℂ. The bov a is called stable if every iterate f^n is analytic in some neighborhood of a (equivalently, suitable iterates extend analytically across a so that a behaves as a "stable" omitted value under iteration).

A Herman ring of f is a periodic Fatou component U of period p ≥ 1 such that U is conformally an annulus and f^p restricted to U is conformally conjugate to an irrational rotation of a standard annulus. The period of the Herman ring is the smallest such p.

It is known that, for any meromorphic function f with a stable Baker omitted value and any fixed integer p ≥ 3, the number of Herman rings of f having period exactly p is finite.

Question: Does there exist a transcendental meromorphic function f possessing a stable Baker omitted value such that f has infinitely many Herman rings whose periods are not bounded (i.e., infinitely many distinct periods occur among the Herman rings of f)? In particular, can such a phenomenon occur in the case where the Baker omitted value is the unique accumulation point of the set of critical values of f?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is explicitly stated as an open problem in the recent survey on Herman rings (2025/2026). Existing results establish only finiteness of p-periodic Herman rings for each fixed p ≥ 3 under a stable bov hypothesis; no construction or obstruction is known for the case of infinitely many Herman rings of varying periods, especially when the bov is the unique accumulation point of critical values.

status_evidence.title: Herman Rings: Structure, Dynamics, and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Whether such a situation can occur, particularly when the bov is the only accumulation point of the critical values, remains an open question.
status_evidence.claim: Stated as an open problem in the survey.

status_evidence.title: Rotation domains and Stable Baker omitted value
status_evidence.snippet: The number of p-periodic Herman rings is shown to be finite for each p ≥ 1.
status_evidence.claim: Background finiteness result for fixed period p.

status_evidence.title: On periods of Herman rings and relevant poles
status_evidence.snippet: A lower bound on the period p of a Herman ring is found in terms of the number of relevant poles.
status_evidence.claim: Related period bounds for Herman rings.
